name: VOD to Media Library
description: VOD → media library bridge. Generates .strm + NFO files from Dispatcharr's VOD catalogue, with optional cron-driven auto-rescan that picks up newly-added episodes.
author: R3XCHRIS

fields.label: About
fields.description:
Turns your Dispatcharr VOD catalogue into a correctly-named media library, delivered two ways from one engine:
  • .strm files on disk — for Jellyfin, Emby, Kodi, ChannelsDVR.
  • a live HTTP mount (rclone) — for Plex, which can't play .strm.
Both share the same title cleaning, folder naming, and playback URLs, so a title lands the same name whichever output you use.

Workflow:
  1. Set the Dispatcharr URL and (for .strm) the root folders below.
  2. Actions → Scan → see catalogue totals.
  3. .strm: Generate Movies / Generate Series (start with Batch Size 10).
  4. Plex: [MOUNT] Enable, then mount with rclone (see [MOUNT] rclone config).

Docs: https://github.com/R3XCHRIS/VOD2MLIB

fields.label: [PATHS & HOSTS]
fields.description: Where to write .strm files and how media servers reach Dispatcharr.

fields.label: Root Folder for Movies
fields.help_text: Path inside the Dispatcharr container where movie folders will be created.

fields.label: Root Folder for Series
fields.help_text: Path inside the Dispatcharr container where series folders will be created.

fields.label: Dispatcharr URL (REQUIRED)
fields.help_text: Required. The externally-reachable URL of your Dispatcharr instance — this gets baked into every .strm file, so it must resolve from wherever your media server runs. localhost works ONLY if the media server is on the same host with shared network namespace; otherwise use a routable LAN IP/hostname. Don't forget to click Save.

fields.label: [MOVIES]
fields.description: Settings for the Generate Movies action.

fields.label: Batch Size (Movies)
fields.help_text: Number of movies to process in this run

fields.label: Generate Movie NFO Files
fields.help_text: Create .nfo metadata files for movies

fields.label: Nest Movies by Category
fields.help_text: Wrap each movie's folder inside a subfolder named by its M3U category. Useful when your provider organises movies by genre. Movies without a category go into a folder named 'Unassigned'. Same content with different categories (e.g. 4K vs HD) gets separate folders intentionally — turn ON Dedupe Movies Across Categories below to suppress this for genre-overlap cases.

fields.label: Dedupe Movies Across Categories
fields.help_text: When `Nest Movies by Category` is ON and a movie is tagged with multiple categories upstream (e.g. 'Action' AND 'Sci-Fi'), write the `.strm` under the first category only (alphabetical by category name) instead of duplicating across all of them. No effect when `Nest Movies by Category` is OFF — in that case multi-category movies already resolve to the same folder. Use this when you want one folder per movie regardless of provider tagging; your media server's genre tags still reflect every category via the NFO. ⚠ MIGRATION: changing this on an already-generated library does NOT remove the old duplicate folders — it just stops creating new ones. To clean up existing duplicates, run `[⚠ DANGER] Clean up Movies` once, then re-generate.

fields.label: Append TMDB ID to folder names
fields.help_text: Append `{tmdb-NNN}` to every Movies and Series folder name when a TMDB ID is known — e.g. `Cool Hand Luke (1967) {tmdb-378}/`. Plex's Personal Media agent and ChannelsDVR's local-media scraper both honour this convention for forced exact matches, which is the safest defence against name collisions and bad metadata scrapes. ⚠ MIGRATION: the plugin does NOT rename existing folders in place — turning this on (or off) for an already-generated library writes the new folder names ALONGSIDE the old ones, creating duplicates. To switch cleanly, run `[⚠ DANGER] Clean up Movies` / `Series` first, then re-generate; or accept the duplicates until the old folders age out.

fields.label: [SERIES]
fields.description: Settings for the Generate Series action.

fields.label: Batch Size (Series)
fields.help_text: Series to process (episodes auto-fetched for each)

fields.label: Generate Series NFO Files
fields.help_text: Create .nfo metadata files for series and episodes

fields.label: Refresh Existing Series (rescan-friendly)
fields.help_text: Re-evaluate series that already have folders, picking up new episodes added upstream AND rewriting existing episode .strm files so they pick up the current Dispatcharr URL. .nfo files (including tvshow.nfo) are only written when missing, so your edits are preserved. Turn ON for cron rescans.

fields.label: Nest Series by Category
fields.help_text: Wrap each series' folder inside a subfolder named by its M3U category. Useful when your provider organises series by genre. Series without a category go into a folder named 'Unassigned'. Same content with different categories gets separate folders intentionally — turn ON Dedupe Series Across Categories below to suppress this for genre-overlap cases.

fields.label: Dedupe Series Across Categories
fields.help_text: When `Nest Series by Category` is ON and a series is tagged with multiple categories upstream, write the series folder + episodes under the first category only (alphabetical by category name) instead of duplicating across all of them. No effect when `Nest Series by Category` is OFF. ⚠ MIGRATION: changing this on an already-generated library does NOT remove the old duplicate folders — run `[⚠ DANGER] Clean up Series` once, then re-generate, to clean them up.

fields.label: [AUTO-RESCAN SCHEDULE]
fields.description: Configure the cron job. Click Apply in the Actions tab to register or update.

fields.label: Auto-Rescan Schedule (cron)
fields.help_text: Standard 5-field cron: 'minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week'. Default '0 3 * * *' = every day at 03:00. Used by 'Apply Schedule'.

fields.label: Schedule Timezone
fields.help_text: IANA timezone name the cron expression is interpreted in (e.g. 'Europe/London', 'America/New_York', 'Australia/Sydney'). Leave empty to use UTC. Affects when the cron fires — '0 3 * * *' in 'Europe/London' means 03:00 London time year-round (handling BST automatically), not 03:00 UTC.

fields.label: Scheduled Action
fields.help_text: Which action the scheduler should run on each tick.

fields.label: [PLEX]
fields.description: Plex delivery of the same library. Plex can't play .strm, so instead the plugin serves your VOD catalogue as a live read-only HTTP filesystem you mount with rclone; Plex reads real, correctly-named files (identical naming to the .strm output) that stream via Dispatcharr's VOD proxy. Click [MOUNT] Enable to start it; the mount runs as a small server inside Dispatcharr and installs uvicorn/fastapi/jinja2 on first enable (the .strm output needs no extra packages). Uses the same Dispatcharr URL as above.

fields.label: Mount HTTP Port
fields.help_text: Port the mount server listens on (inside the container; publish it so rclone can reach it). rclone connects here; the Dispatcharr URL above is the playback redirect target. Default 8889.

fields.label: Mount Authentication (Token-based)
fields.help_text: Require a Dispatcharr API key on every mount request. Enable if the port is exposed beyond a trusted network. When ON, add the API key to the rclone config's headers line.

fields.label: Mount Size-Hydration Concurrency
fields.help_text: Parallel fetches the mount uses to backfill real file sizes from your provider (Plex needs true sizes to play). 0 disables hydration (only already-sized titles show). Default 8.

fields.label: Mount: Full size-sync on enable
fields.help_text: On [MOUNT] Enable, kick off a one-time size hydration pass so titles become visible to Plex sooner.

fields.label: Mount Hydration Times (24h)
fields.help_text: Comma-separated HHMM times to run a daily size-hydration pass (e.g. '0300,1500'). Empty disables the schedule.

fields.label: Mount Hydration Timezone
fields.help_text: IANA timezone for the hydration times above. Empty = UTC.

actions.label: [LIBRARY] Catalogue snapshot
actions.description: Count unique Movies and Series in the Dispatcharr database. Read-only.

actions.label: [GENERATE] Movies
actions.description: Process movies per Batch Size. Existing .strm files are skipped.

actions.label: [GENERATE] Series
actions.description: Create episode .strm files. See 'Refresh Existing Series' setting.

actions.label: [GENERATE] Full rescan
actions.description: Rescan then force regenerate Movies + Series.

confirm.title: Run full rescan now?
confirm.message: Full rescan walks every Movie and every Series, re-fetching episode lists from the M3U source and writing any missing files. On large catalogues this can take many minutes. The cron schedule already runs this action nightly — only click here for an immediate refresh.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Show status
actions.description: Show registered cron, last run, and total runs.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Test fire now
actions.description: Fire the scheduled task immediately. Verifies the cron pipeline.

confirm.title: Fire scheduled task now?
confirm.message: Runs the same action the cron will fire (with the snapshotted settings) right now. Useful to verify the pipeline works. May take many minutes depending on the action.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Apply / Update
actions.description: Register or update the cron task. Re-click after changing any setting.

confirm.title: Remove auto-rescan schedule?
confirm.message: This unregisters the periodic task. You can re-create it any time with Apply.

actions.label: [⚠ DANGER] Clean up Movies
actions.description: Delete plugin .strm/.nfo from Movies root. User files preserved.

confirm.title: Delete generated movie files?
confirm.message: This deletes every .strm and .nfo file this plugin created under your Movies root. User-added files (subtitles, posters, custom .nfo) in those folders are preserved. Continue?

actions.label: [⚠ DANGER] Clean up Series
actions.description: Delete plugin .strm/.nfo from Series root. User files preserved.

confirm.title: Delete generated series files?
confirm.message: This deletes every .strm and .nfo file this plugin created under your Series root. User-added files in those folders are preserved. Continue?

actions.label: [MOUNT] Enable Plex mount
actions.description: Start the HTTP filesystem server for rclone/Plex. Installs uvicorn/fastapi/jinja2 on first run.

actions.label: [MOUNT] Status
actions.description: Show mount server state, visible title counts, and hydration progress.

actions.label: [MOUNT] rclone config
actions.description: Where to get the paste-ready rclone remote for the mount.

actions.label: [MOUNT] Hydrate sizes now
actions.description: Trigger an immediate size-hydration pass so more titles become visible to Plex.

actions.label: [MOUNT] Disable Plex mount
actions.description: Stop the HTTP filesystem server. The .strm generator is unaffected.
